domain_description: Rosenshine's Principles of Instruction in practice — opening a lesson with review, modelling expert thinking aloud, building I Do / We Do / You Do sequences, and designing scaffolded practice. All interventions cross-referenced to peer-reviewed meta-analyses where one exists.

skills.display_title: Explicit Instruction Sequence Builder (I Do / We Do / You Do)
skills.description: Build a complete explicit instruction sequence — teacher modelling, guided practice with prompts and corrections, then independent practice — so students see expert thinking, rehearse it with support, and practise it alone.
skills.implementation_cost_rationale: Designing a quality I Do / We Do / You Do sequence requires real prep work per topic — script the modelling, anticipate misconceptions to address during guided practice, calibrate independent tasks for the right level of challenge. No materials or training needed once teachers know the pattern.

skills.description: Design a 3-5 minute opening routine that activates prior knowledge, retrieves yesterday's key content, and bridges to today's lesson — turning the first few minutes from settling time into learning time.
skills.implementation_cost_rationale: A 3-5 minute opening routine takes minutes to design and minutes to deliver per lesson; no materials beyond a slide or prompt, no training beyond awareness that retrieval-anchored openings beat content-recap openings. The cost is the recurring discipline, not setup.

skills.description: Generate a scaffolded sequence of practice problems with graduated difficulty and strategic variability — starting from worked examples, fading scaffolds through partially-worked problems, ending in independent practice.
skills.implementation_cost_rationale: Designing a high-quality faded practice sequence requires real PCK — anticipating where students need scaffolds, calibrating fade rate, generating worked solutions plus problem variants. Once designed, the sequence is reusable across cohorts; AI generation accelerates but doesn't eliminate the design work.
